alternatives_considered: no floor at all, which would accept a divider whose off level sits in the millivolts and reads noise as signal
requirements.name: above_a_fifth_of_the_nominal_supply
requirements.rationale: the brief requires a stated threshold but no floor; a fifth of the minimum supply keeps the off level far enough from the reference that ground shift and coupled noise on field wiring cannot read as asserted
requirements.statement: each input's guaranteed off threshold at the terminal stays above a fifth of the minimum declared supply

requirements.name: above_the_clamping_voltage
requirements.rationale: 'clamped below the rating of everything behind the input', inverted per part: the highest level the clamp can present is its clamping voltage at rated pulse current, and each exposed part's rating must clear it
requirements.statement: every part the transient reaches while the input clamp conducts is rated above the clamp's maximum clamping voltage

requirements.name: above_the_declared_bus_fault_voltage
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the withstood fault voltage to be stated and to cover a bus line shorted to ground or to the node's own 24 V; the declared figure is the input range's maximum, and both parts on the bus must stand it off
requirements.statement: the transceiver and the bus protector each stand off the declared bus fault voltage

requirements.name: above_the_declared_input_maximum
requirements.rationale: the brief requires 'every part in that path rated above it with margin' over a stated range; the range is this design's declaration (18-30 V, registered as a statement), and each part's rating is read from its own frozen datasheet
requirements.statement: every part standing across the input rail or in the path from it is rated above the declared input maximum

requirements.name: above_the_enable_threshold
requirements.rationale: an enable that does not clear its threshold at the input minimum is a board that does not start inside its declared range; the datasheet states only a typical threshold, which the claim records as its assumption
requirements.statement: the converter's enable divider clears its rising threshold at the declared input minimum

requirements.name: above_the_regulator_floor
requirements.rationale: the linear regulator only regulates while its input clears its output by its dropout; the datasheet states dropout only at 1 mA, so the figure used is this design's declared bound at the logic load - an assumption registered separately
requirements.statement: the intermediate rail stays above the logic rail's maximum plus the regulator's declared dropout bound

requirements.name: above_the_steady_level_across_the_part
requirements.rationale: the net levels are bounded rail-by-rail from the supply model; transient levels are the clamp claims' business, and this sweep compares steady levels only
requirements.statement: every capacitor is rated above the highest steady level across it

requirements.name: above_the_sum_of_the_channel_ratings
requirements.rationale: the field return concentrates every channel's current in the connector; its rating must clear the sum
requirements.statement: the field connector's contact rating covers the sum of the channel ratings

alternatives_considered: relying on the controller's typical hysteresis, which is not a guaranteed figure and vanishes in the divider ratio
requirements.name: at_least_one_volt_at_the_terminal
requirements.rationale: the brief requires stated hysteresis but no figure; one volt at the terminal is the bound this design declares, computed from the controller's guaranteed threshold separation referred back through the divider rather than from the datasheet's typical hysteresis figure
requirements.statement: each input's guaranteed hysteresis, referred to the terminal, is at least one volt

requirements.name: at_or_above_a_characterised_drive
requirements.rationale: an on-resistance is only a datasheet fact at the gate drive the datasheet characterises; every drop computed from it requires the gate to actually reach that point
requirements.statement: each FET gate is driven at or above a gate-source voltage its on-resistance is characterised at

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_controller_supply_minimum
requirements.rationale: the brief demands working rails without naming figures; the figures are the controller datasheet's characterised window
requirements.statement: the logic rail stays at or above the controller's characterised supply minimum

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_declared_discharge_level
requirements.rationale: the brief requires meeting 'the declared IEC 61000-4-2 level'; the level is this design's declaration (8 kV contact, powered, registered as a statement), and both documents state device-level ratings - a system discharge result for this board remains a physical test
requirements.statement: the bus protector and the transceiver are each rated at or above the declared IEC 61000-4-2 contact discharge level

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_declared_input_maximum
requirements.rationale: a clamp whose stand-off sits below the working rail conducts continuously; the brief's protection requirements imply a stand-off floor at the declared maximum
requirements.statement: every clamp's stand-off voltage covers the declared input maximum so protection never conducts in normal operation

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_planned_build_quantity
requirements.rationale: the planned build (registered as a statement) is a requirement on availability, not only on the design; the stock figure is the catalogue reading at its recorded retrieval date, not a reservation
requirements.statement: the catalogue's recorded stock covers the planned build quantity for every ordered part

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_sum_of_the_channel_ratings
requirements.rationale: all four channels at their rated current pass the fuse; its hold current is read from the datasheet's derating table at the declared ambient, not interpolated
requirements.statement: the resettable fuse holds the sum of the channel ratings at the declared maximum ambient

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_transceiver_interface_minimum
requirements.rationale: the transceiver's logic-side interface has its own supply window, separate from its bus-side supply; both have to be met for the controller and transceiver to exchange levels
requirements.statement: the logic rail stays at or above the transceiver's I/O supply minimum

requirements.name: at_or_above_the_transceiver_supply_minimum
requirements.rationale: the brief requires that 'the transceiver shall get the supply voltage its datasheet requires'; the datasheet window's lower edge is the requirement, evaluated with the converter's reference and the feedback divider at their worst corner
requirements.statement: the intermediate rail stays at or above the transceiver's supply minimum at the tolerance corner that lowers it

requirements.name: at_or_below_the_controller_supply_maximum
requirements.rationale: the upper edge of the same characterised window, at the top of the regulator's accuracy
requirements.statement: the logic rail stays at or below the controller's characterised supply maximum

requirements.name: at_or_below_the_minimum_declared_input_supply
requirements.rationale: the brief requires a stated threshold; for the input to read an asserted line at the bottom of the declared range, the worst-corner on threshold must sit at or below it
requirements.statement: each input's guaranteed on threshold at the terminal sits at or below the minimum declared supply

requirements.name: at_or_below_the_transceiver_qualified_rate
requirements.rationale: the brief requires 'the maximum qualified data-phase rate stated'; the stated rate (registered as a statement) is qualified against the G-variant datasheet's minimum transmitted bit time
requirements.statement: the declared data-phase rate stays at or below the rate the fitted transceiver variant's bit-timing specification supports

requirements.name: at_or_below_the_transceiver_supply_maximum
requirements.rationale: the same datasheet window's upper edge, evaluated at the opposite corner of the reference and divider tolerances
requirements.statement: the intermediate rail stays at or below the transceiver's supply maximum at the tolerance corner that raises it

alternatives_considered: checking merely 'less than the whole difference', which any working converter satisfies vacuously and which would therefore judge nothing
requirements.name: below_a_quarter_of_the_whole_input_to_output_difference_at_load
requirements.rationale: the brief forbids dissipating the full input-to-output difference at load; 'not the full difference' needs a checkable margin, and a quarter is the bound this design declares. The switched topology beats it by construction - the only linear element drops the intermediate-to-logic difference, never input-to-logic
requirements.statement: the linear stage dissipates less than a quarter of what dissipating the whole input-to-output difference at load would

alternatives_considered: two discrete single-line devices, whose mismatch would be the difference of two independent parts' tolerances and could not be bounded to this level from their datasheets
requirements.name: below_a_tenth_of_a_picofarad
requirements.rationale: the brief requires protection 'balanced line to line' without a number; a tenth of a picofarad is the bound this design declares, met by fitting one dual device whose datasheet states the variation between its own two lines - a figure the datasheet gives as a typical, which the claim records
requirements.statement: the bus protector's line-to-line capacitance mismatch stays below a tenth of a picofarad

requirements.name: below_the_controller_supply_absolute_maximum
requirements.rationale: the same unpowered case bounds where the rail settles: the clamp current through the bleed's high tolerance corner must leave the rail below the controller's absolute maximum
requirements.statement: the unpowered logic rail, lifted by the input clamps against the bleed, stays below the controller's absolute-maximum supply

requirements.name: below_the_converter_current_limit
requirements.rationale: a peak that reaches the limit turns the limit into the regulator; the design point stays below the datasheet's minimum limit so regulation is by feedback, not by the protection
requirements.statement: the converter's peak current stays below its own minimum current limit

requirements.name: below_the_inductor_heat_rating_current
requirements.rationale: the thermal rating bounds continuous current; the DC component alone is compared, and the omitted ripple share is recorded on the claim
requirements.statement: the converter's DC output current stays below the inductor's heat-rating current

requirements.name: below_the_inductor_saturation_current
requirements.rationale: an inductor past saturation stops being the part the converter's stability and current limit were computed with; the peak is the load bound plus half the worst-corner ripple
requirements.statement: the converter's peak inductor current stays below the inductor's saturation rating at the tolerance corner that maximises ripple

requirements.name: below_the_switch_breakdown_voltage
requirements.rationale: the brief requires inductive turn-off clamped within the switch's rating; the clamp's worst clamping voltage at rated pulse current is what the drain sees, and it must clear the FET's minimum breakdown
requirements.statement: the output clamp's maximum clamping voltage stays below the switch's minimum breakdown

requirements.name: below_the_switch_threshold_voltage
requirements.rationale: the brief requires every output 'off from power-on until firmware drives it'; after reset the controller leaves the port floating, so the pull-down must hold the gate below the FET's minimum threshold against the pin's leakage
requirements.statement: each output gate, with nothing driving it, stays below the switch's minimum threshold

requirements.name: below_the_transceiver_bus_fault_rating
requirements.rationale: a protector that clamps above what the transceiver survives protects nothing; the clamp ceiling is the transceiver's fault rating
requirements.statement: the bus protector clamps below the transceiver's own fault rating

requirements.name: bus_conductors_adjacent_with_nothing_between
requirements.statement: CANH and CANL occupy adjacent contacts of the bus connector with no other contact between them

requirements.name: each_gate_reaches_one_switch_and_its_own_pull_down
requirements.rationale: the brief requires outputs that 'switch independently' and are off from power-on; the netlist condition is one switch and one pull-down per gate net, shared with nothing
requirements.statement: each output gate net reaches exactly one switch and its own pull-down to the reference

requirements.name: each_termination_leg_passes_through_its_own_link
requirements.rationale: the brief requires termination 'switchable to fully removed without unsoldering parts'; with a split termination that is only true if BOTH legs break - pulling both links removes the differential load rather than leaving one line loaded against the centre capacitor
requirements.statement: each termination leg passes through its own removable link, one per side of the pair

requirements.name: equals_the_declared_position_count
requirements.rationale: a contract declaring more or fewer positions than the part has is a contract about a different connector
requirements.statement: each connector's physical position count matches its declared pin order

requirements.name: equals_the_declared_transient_clamp
requirements.rationale: the brief requires transients 'clamped below the rating of everything behind the input'; the level everything is compared against must be the fitted part's own worst figure, not a chosen number, or the comparison floats free of the hardware
requirements.statement: the declared transient clamp level equals the fitted input suppressor's maximum clamping voltage at its rated pulse current

requirements.name: equals_the_package_terminal_count
requirements.rationale: a land pattern with the wrong pad count cannot carry the package; the count is compared against each part's land-pattern document
requirements.statement: each footprint's pad count matches its package's terminal count

requirements.name: every_connector_pin_carries_its_declared_function
requirements.rationale: the connector contracts are the design's declaration of what mates with what; a pin on the wrong net is a mating failure the netlist can catch before any board exists
requirements.statement: every connector pin lands on the net its declared contract names

requirements.name: every_entering_conductor_carries_a_clamp_or_a_recorded_reason
requirements.rationale: the brief demands ESD protection at the bus connector and transient protection on the input; the design generalises that discipline to every entering conductor so an unprotected line is a named decision, never an omission
requirements.statement: every conductor entering the board reaches a suppressor, or is recorded exempt with a reason

requirements.name: every_input_has_a_pull_down_to_the_reference
requirements.rationale: the brief requires 'a defined state with its terminal open'; the mechanism is each divider's lower element returning to the reference, which is a checkable netlist fact
requirements.statement: every input divider returns to the reference so an open terminal reads de-asserted

requirements.name: every_required_net_reaches_a_probe
requirements.statement: every rail, both bus lines and the transceiver's TXD/RXD pair reach a test point

requirements.name: every_terminal_named_by_a_package_map_is_on_a_net_or_declared_no_connect
requirements.rationale: a mapped terminal on no net is either a missing connection or a missing declaration; both are defects the netlist can name
requirements.statement: every terminal a package map names is on a net or declared no-connect

requirements.name: matches_the_declared_through_hole_count
requirements.rationale: through-hole count drives the hand-soldering line of the assembly quote; the policy (registered as a statement) declares it so the quote is priced from the design, not discovered
requirements.statement: the number of through-hole parts matches the declared assembly policy

requirements.name: no_controller_pin_on_a_bus_conductor
requirements.statement: no controller pin lands on CANH or CANL; the controller reaches the bus only through the transceiver

requirements.name: the_extraction_was_taken_from_the_committed_board
requirements.rationale: every copper claim reads the extraction; if the board was edited after the trace, those claims describe copper that is no longer there, so the digest match is the first claim and gates the rest
requirements.statement: the committed extraction describes the committed board file, by digest

alternatives_considered: judging only the bare resistor tolerance stack, which would silently widen with any part substitution
requirements.name: within_five_percent_of_the_nominal_termination
requirements.rationale: the brief requires 'a nominal 120 ohm differential load' without a tolerance; a nominal needs a checkable window. Five percent holds the two-leg stack at every corner of the fitted parts' tolerance and is declared once, so a substitution that widened the stack would fail here instead of shipping
requirements.statement: the enabled termination presents the nominal 120 ohm differential load within five percent at every tolerance corner

alternatives_considered: no declared drop budget, which would let the board consume the field devices' margin invisibly
requirements.name: within_one_volt_of_the_declared_input_minimum
requirements.rationale: the brief requires parts rated over a stated range but sets no budget for what the board's own path may drop; one volt at full load is the bound this design declares, spent across the fuse, the blocking device and the board's copper - first priced from the copper budget, then re-checked against the routed copper's extracted resistance
requirements.statement: the field supply at the connector stays within one volt of the declared input minimum at full load

requirements.name: within_the_budgeted_copper_drop
requirements.rationale: the same check per channel: the extracted conductor resistance times the rated channel current against the budget times that current
requirements.statement: each output conductor's drop at its rated current stays within the budgeted copper drop

requirements.name: within_the_controller_injection_limit
requirements.rationale: on the negative side the controller's own structure clamps the pin at the reference and the series element bounds the injected current, which must stay inside the datasheet's per-pin injection limit
requirements.statement: each input's negative-extreme injection stays within the controller's per-pin limit

requirements.name: within_the_controller_input_voltage_rating
requirements.rationale: the brief requires each input to survive the maximum rated input continuously; on the positive side the clamp diode holds the pin one forward drop above the logic rail, which must sit inside the pin's tolerant-input rating
requirements.statement: each input pin stays within its rating at the positive extreme of the declared range

requirements.name: within_the_controller_maximum_critical_transconductance
requirements.rationale: the controller can only start a crystal whose critical transconductance is inside what its oscillator can supply; whether a gain margin beyond the stated maximum is required is a vendor application-note question this board does not resolve, so oscillator start-up remains a physical test
requirements.statement: the crystal's critical transconductance, computed at its worst resistance and capacitance corner, stays within the controller's stated maximum

requirements.name: within_the_controller_oscillator_range
requirements.rationale: the controller's clock tree supports a stated HSE range; a crystal outside it is a part the reference manual does not describe
requirements.statement: the crystal's frequency sits inside the controller's supported external-oscillator range

requirements.name: within_the_controller_total_injection_limit
requirements.rationale: the per-pin limit is not the whole story: the datasheet also bounds the total, and the worst case is every input at the negative extreme at once
requirements.statement: the sum of every input's injection stays within the controller's total injection limit

requirements.name: within_the_converter_output_rating
requirements.rationale: the load bound takes the transceiver driving a dominant bit into the lowest load its datasheet characterises, continuously, plus everything behind the regulator
requirements.statement: the intermediate rail's bounded worst-case load stays within the converter's output current rating

requirements.name: within_the_converter_pin_rating
requirements.rationale: the enable divider sees the clamped transient; the pin's absolute maximum has to cover the divider's output at that level at the corner that raises it
requirements.statement: the enable pin stays within its absolute maximum while the input is at the transient clamp level

requirements.name: within_the_declared_board_copper_budget
requirements.rationale: every pre-layout rail claim priced the board's conductors from a declared budget because no copper existed yet; the routed copper's traced resistance is compared back against that budget so the price paid is checked rather than trusted
requirements.statement: each field conductor's extracted resistance stays within the declared board copper budget

alternatives_considered: adopting a cable-system capacitance allocation from a CAN standard, which is not frozen evidence in this repository
requirements.name: within_the_declared_bus_capacitance_budget
requirements.rationale: the brief requires protection to 'add no more capacitance than the qualified rate allows'; what the rate allows is not a frozen specification figure, so the board declares the budget: five percent of a bit time at the declared data-phase rate through the load the transceiver's datasheet characterises its outputs into
requirements.statement: the protection adds no more capacitance to the bus than five percent of a data-phase bit time through the transceiver's characterised load

alternatives_considered: adopting a vendor application note's figure, which is not frozen evidence in this repository and could not be cited
requirements.name: within_the_declared_oscillator_budget
requirements.rationale: no CAN specification clause is frozen in this repository that states a tolerance for this rate, so the board declares one: the classical requirement that two nodes' clocks not drift more than a fraction of a bit over the longest unsynchronised stretch, halved per node. Initial tolerance, temperature, one year of ageing and the load network's pulling are summed arithmetically
requirements.statement: the crystal's worst-case frequency error, pulling included, stays within the declared per-node tolerance budget

requirements.name: within_the_diode_average_current_rating
requirements.rationale: the diode conducts for the off fraction of each cycle; its average current is the output current times that fraction at the corner that maximises it
requirements.statement: the catch diode's average current at worst duty stays within its forward-current rating

requirements.name: within_the_fuse_maximum_fault_current
requirements.rationale: the board's own series resistance is milliohms, so the fault current a short draws is set by the installation; the board declares the prospective current the installation must respect (registered as a statement), and the fuse must be rated for it
requirements.statement: the declared prospective fault current stays within the fuse's maximum interrupt rating

requirements.name: within_the_gate_source_rating
requirements.rationale: the brief requires reverse polarity 'shall not damage the board or latch'; the blocking FET's gate sees the zener's clamp level, and the worst case for the rating is the zener's maximum
requirements.statement: the reverse-blocking device's gate clamp holds its gate-source voltage within the device's rating at the top of the zener tolerance

requirements.name: within_the_link_current_rating
requirements.rationale: the links sit in the differential path, so the dominant drive current and the bounded bus-fault current both pass through them; a contact rated below either is a switch that fails closed
requirements.statement: the termination links carry their normal and bus-fault currents within the link's contact rating

requirements.name: within_the_package_dissipation
requirements.rationale: the brief requires the stated per-channel current 'with all four on'; the package figures used are the datasheet ratings at their own 25 C reference, so this establishes dissipation against the rating, not a junction temperature
requirements.statement: no package dissipates more than its datasheet rating with every channel conducting at once

requirements.name: within_the_regulator_output_rating
requirements.rationale: the load bound sums the controller at its datasheet maximum, the transceiver's interface supply, the indicator and the rail bleed
requirements.statement: the logic rail's bounded worst-case load stays within the regulator's output current rating

requirements.name: within_the_resistor_power_rating
requirements.rationale: each steady dissipation is bounded with the whole named level across the element, which overstates dividers; the termination legs are additionally bounded under the transceiver-limited bus fault
requirements.statement: every resistor carrying steady current dissipates within its rating, and the termination legs survive a bus fault

requirements.name: within_the_switch_continuous_current
requirements.rationale: the declared per-channel rating (registered as a statement) must sit inside the FET's continuous current rating for the channel rating to be the board's and not the transistor's
requirements.statement: each channel's rated current stays within the switch's continuous drain rating

requirements.name: within_the_zener_power_rating
requirements.rationale: the clamp carries the divider current whenever the input is up; its steady dissipation is bounded at the declared maximum with the series element at its low tolerance corner
requirements.statement: the gate-clamp zener's dissipation at the declared input maximum stays within its power rating

requirements.name: within_what_the_rail_bleed_alone_sinks
requirements.rationale: with the board unpowered and every input at the positive extreme, the clamp diodes feed the logic rail; the bleed element must sink all of it or the rail floats up on an unpowered board
requirements.statement: the input clamps' worst-case back-fed current is less than what the rail bleed alone sinks

alternatives_considered: second-side placement, rejected because nothing on this board needs it and it adds a setup to the quote
statements.name: assembly_policy
statements.rationale: a single placement side and an explicit through-hole count keep the assembly quote priced from the design; the count is judged by its own claim
statements.statement: assembly is one reflow of the front side, with the through-hole connectors hand-soldered and counted

alternatives_considered: 2 Mbit/s data phase, rejected as leaving qualified transceiver capability unstated for no margin gain
statements.name: bus_rate_declaration
statements.rationale: the brief requires the maximum qualified data-phase rate to be stated; the arbitration rate is the classical CAN ceiling, and the data-phase rate is the one the fitted transceiver variant's datasheet characterises
statements.statement: the node is qualified at 1 Mbit/s arbitration and 5 Mbit/s data phase

alternatives_considered: a higher per-channel rating, rejected because the fuse's hold current at the declared ambient would not cover the sum
statements.name: channel_current_rating
statements.rationale: the brief requires 'the stated per-channel current with all four on' but leaves the figure open; a quarter ampere per channel keeps the four-channel sum inside the resettable fuse's held current at the declared ambient with the fuse read from its derating table
statements.statement: each field output is rated at 0.25 A with all four channels conducting at once

statements.invalidated_by: a measured efficiency below 75 percent at the board's own load, which would raise the input current above the figures used
statements.name: converter_efficiency_bound
statements.reason: the input-current bound every input-path figure uses divides the output power by a deliberately pessimistic efficiency; the datasheet's curves sit well above it but are not frozen as parameters
statements.statement: the converter's efficiency is at least 75 percent at the loads this board presents

alternatives_considered: 15 kV air discharge as the headline figure, rejected because contact discharge is the harsher and better-specified test at the same nominal level
statements.name: esd_level_declaration
statements.rationale: the brief requires meeting 'the declared level' and leaves the level to the design; 8 kV contact is the level both fitted parts' datasheets state device ratings at or above
statements.statement: the declared bus discharge level is 8 kV IEC 61000-4-2 contact, powered

alternatives_considered: a wider 9-36 V industrial range, rejected because the input clamp's stand-off and the converter's maximum rating would both need different parts
statements.name: input_range_declaration
statements.rationale: the brief requires the continuous 24 V input range to be stated; 18 V is what the field supply may sag to and still be inside the declared range, 30 V is what every part behind the terminal is rated above and what the input clamp stands off
statements.statement: the declared continuous input range is 18 to 30 V

alternatives_considered: 25 C, rejected as a bench figure that would overstate the fuse's held current in any real enclosure
statements.name: maximum_ambient
statements.rationale: the resettable fuse's hold current and the controller's supply current are both temperature-dependent; every figure used is read from its datasheet at or above this ambient, so the declared ambient is the temperature the ratings are actually established at
statements.statement: the board's ratings are claimed at a maximum ambient of 60 C

alternatives_considered: a transceiver without the G qualification, rejected because the declared data-phase rate could not be stated from its datasheet
an MCU with external CAN controller, rejected as a second device and a second clock domain the brief's integrated-CAN-FD condition excludes
statements.name: mcu_and_transceiver_selection
statements.rationale: the brief leaves both open subject to an integrated CAN-FD controller, the declared I/O count, and the stated rate and fault ratings. The STM32G431 carries an FDCAN controller and enough I/O; the TCAN1042's G variant is the one whose datasheet specifies bit timing at a 200 ns transmitted bit, which is what qualifies the declared 5 Mbit/s data phase, and its fault rating covers the node's own 24 V shorted to a bus line
statements.statement: the controller is an STM32G431 and the transceiver a TCAN1042 G-variant

alternatives_considered: assuming a field-wiring resistance to bound the fault current, rejected because nothing in the design controls the wiring
statements.name: prospective_fault_current
statements.rationale: the fuse cannot be shown to survive more than its own maximum fault current, and the board's own series resistance is far too small to limit a stiff source; the board therefore declares the figure the installation has to respect rather than assuming a wiring resistance that would make the question go away
statements.statement: the installation must not present more than 30 A of prospective fault current at the board's terminals

statements.invalidated_by: a measured dropout above the declared bound at the logic load, which would push the regulator out of regulation inside the declared input range
statements.name: regulator_dropout_bound
statements.reason: the datasheet states dropout only at 1 mA; the logic load is higher, so the bound the intermediate rail is judged against is a declared figure, not a datasheet limit
statements.statement: the regulator's dropout at the logic-rail load is within the declared bound used by the rail claims

alternatives_considered: an analog switch or relay under MCU control, rejected because its on-resistance sits inside the 120 ohm tolerance window and its capacitance inside the bus budget, both of which are already declared tight
statements.name: termination_control
statements.rationale: the brief leaves manual versus MCU-controlled switching open. Links satisfy 'switchable to fully removed without unsoldering parts' with zero switch elements in the differential path: an electronic switch would put its own resistance and capacitance into the termination and both would need their own qualification against the balance and capacitance bounds
statements.statement: termination switches manually, by two removable links, not under MCU control
